title: Batcher cold-start amplification recovery protocol
creator: Amina Patel
description: Follow-up ticket for the 2026-03-08 production incident where an aggressive slot-reclamation heuristic combined with a new batching timer caused prolonged batch formation stalls during cold starts. Resulted in multi-minute tail-latency amplification for some customers and unfair queueing of short requests.
background: During a routine rollout of the slot-evaporation optimization (feature flag enabled in runtime-1.22), we observed a high-frequency scenario where workers aggressively released idle batch slots. Under cold-start load patterns this produced long periods where no full batches formed, amplifying latency for affected requests and causing fairness regressions across tenants.
timeline: 2026-03-08 02:12 UTC: Canary rollout of slot-evaporation starts (10% of hosts).
2026-03-08 02:37 UTC: First spike in tail P99 observed for generation routes; ops alert fired.
2026-03-08 02:45 UTC: Oncall identifies prolonged empty windows in batch-formation metric and elevated 'slot_reclaim' events.
2026-03-08 03:01 UTC: Emergency rollback of slot-evaporation flag to previous behavior across canaries; tail latency returns toward baseline over ~6 minutes.
2026-03-08 04:20 UTC: Full rollback confirmed; incident declared resolved at 04:35 UTC.
2026-03-09 10:00 UTC: Post-incident triage and data capture; heap of traces exported to S3 and linked below.
impact: Several customer-facing production clusters experienced sustained P99 generation latency increases from ~220ms baseline to 4–7s for affected request classes. Approximately 3% of requests across canaries and early rollout zones hit the degraded behavior during the window. No data loss, but customer SLA alerts were triggered for multiple enterprise tenants.
detection: Automated SLO monitors for P99 token-latency and a synthetic canary test triggered PagerDuty. Oncall used the batch-formation and slot_reclaim metrics dashboards to correlate unusual spikes in slot reclamation events with stretches of zero batch completions.
root_cause: A change in slot-evaporation heuristic reduced the minimum hold-time for idle slots and introduced a race with the continuous batcher timer. Under cold-start or bursty request arrivals, slots were reclaimed before the batcher timer could aggregate sufficient requests to form efficient batches. This produced repeated micro-windows where no batch was emitted, increasing tail latency and stratifying which request sizes got scheduled (favoring already-warmed large KV-cache paths). Additionally, the rollout lacked a synthetic cold-start workload in the canary gating criteria.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back the slot-evaporation heuristic to the prior hold-time within 20 minutes of detection. Temporarily disabled the new 'aggressive_reclaim' flag in all regions. Increased alerting sensitivity on batch-formation-empty-window rate.
mitigations_applied: manual-throttle: limited concurrent rollout velocity for future changes to slot heuristics
action_items: A1: Add deterministic cold-start canary: create a synthetic workload that injects cold-KV and sparse arrival patterns into canary pool. Owner: Diego Ramos. Due: 2026-03-20.
A2: Rework slot reclaim heuristic: implement minimum hold-time and conditional backoff when batcher queue depth < X for Y ms. Owner: Priya Nambiar. Estimate: 5 pts. Due: 2026-03-28.

A3: Fairness guardrail: add a short-request priority token that ensures one slot reserved every N cycles for small requests when batch formation stalls. Owner: Marcus Li. Estimate: 3 pts. Due: 2026-04-03.
A4: Add chaos test: simulate slot-reclaim race under cold-start with randomized timers in integration test harness. Owner: QA team (lead: Sofia Kim). Due: 2026-03-25.

A5: New observability slices: per-tenant batch formation success rate, slot_reclaim latency histogram, and a heatmap of empty-window duration. Owner: Observability (lead: Elena Ortiz). Due: 2026-03-18.
A6: Automated rollback gate: require synthetic-cold-start pass before any slot-related rollout progresses beyond canary. Owner: Release Eng. Due: 2026-03-22.
A7: Regression test: add unit/regression tests for batcher timer/slot interactions and KV-cache warm-path bias. Owner: Diego Ramos. Estimate: 2 pts. Due: 2026-03-17.
A8: Customer communications: prepare incident summary and outreach for impacted enterprise customers. Owner: CS (lead: Anya Feldman). Due: 2026-03-15.
followups: F1: Run a 72-hour soak with adjusted heuristics on a dedicated test cluster and validate SLOs under synthetic cold-start traffic.
F2: Evaluate whether burst-aware batching (shorter per-slot timers under low-pressure but with reserved fallback) reduces cost or increases variance for normal traffic.
F3: Revisit rollout policy to require two-phase canary (warm and cold synthetic workloads) for any low-level runtime changes affecting batching or KV cache mechanics.
notes: Operational lesson: low-level runtime heuristics interact with scheduling timers in non-obvious ways; we need gating that includes behavioral synthetic tests, not just traffic-volume testing.

Engineering tradeoff: increasing minimum slot hold-time slightly raises average cost per token but dramatically reduces tail risk under cold starts; we recommend making this tunable per-customer tier.
Security note: no secret data was exposed; logs and traces collected were scrubbed before sharing with customers.
